The proceedings paper exists at the cited venue and develops graph-product machinery for induced and semi-induced matching hardness; its primary full theorem text was access-restricted, so the exact Theorem 5.9 formulation remains source-verification pending.

The published paper establishes bounded-degree Max-2-CSP and claw-free independent-set hardness under randomized reductions, including UGC and unconditional variants; it is relevant to randomized-reduction bookkeeping, not to DTE-risk calibration.

The abstract studies no-interference finite-population ATE minimax design and estimation under bounded outcomes, first for a broad affine class and then extending to arbitrary estimators; the cited theorem-number and finite-convex-program wording require direct full-text verification.

For bounded no-interference potential outcomes, the paper exactly reduces the all-design/all-estimator minimax problem to a low-dimensional binomial experiment and gives an attaining Bernoulli design with nonlinear estimator.
The paper studies full-class minimax estimation subject to design-unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, so it does not eliminate biased nonlinear estimators in the unrestricted DTE game.
